text: Felix Nakamura plans the classical baseline: brute-force every possible 4-of-12 combination, exactly, no shortcuts.
495 combinations total, checked exhaustively -- this makes the result exact ground truth, not an estimate to argue over.
QAOA doesn't return one answer -- it returns a probability distribution over 4,096 possible bitstrings, some far more likely than others.
Success gets defined now, before any results exist: does the true optimum land near the top of the sampling, and how close is the value gap.
Next: planning the path from the ideal, noiseless simulator to real ibm_brisbane hardware.
